A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AdaConG with the same authors, core framework and evaluation families. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original distillation and semi-supervised classification accuracies, gridworld learning curves, autonomous-driving results and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments with MSE guidance and direct nonconformity-score weighting.

M1.justification: V4 adds an evaluated SSL variant using MSE between strongly and weakly augmented logits instead of cross-entropy against pseudo-labels (Section 4, Table 3). The core conformal weighting mechanism remains unchanged. Expanded RL calibration details do not independently establish that its implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100 distillation, CIFAR-10/100 and STL-10 semi-supervised classification, Lava 1/Lava 2/Door navigation, and SullyChen steering. The new loss and calibration ablations use retained datasets and tasks without adding populations or environmental scenarios.

E2.justification: V4 introduces direct nonconformity-score weighting as an evaluated KD comparator in Appendix A.1.5 and Table 7. Existing KD, SSL, navigation and driving comparator sets remain. Reordering Table 1 and changing the entropy citation do not establish different comparison methods.

E3.justification: V4 adds an SSL experiment using strong/weak-logit MSE at the existing CIFAR-100 label budgets and a KD control bypassing conformal quantile/set construction. Previously stated splits, noise corruptions, architectures and training budgets remain unchanged; newly specified RL calibration settings are documentation additions.

E4.justification: Two targeted ablations are added: sensitivity to the SSL guidance-loss formulation (Table 3) and the benefit of conformalizing nonconformity scores (Table 7). Existing temperature/error-rate sensitivity studies, hard-weighting tests, navigation uncertainty analysis and computational comparison are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report four-run means and standard deviations for KD/SSL and ten random seeds for navigation. The additional results follow existing reporting practices; no new confidence intervals, significance tests or increased run counts are reported.

E6.justification: V4 Table 3 adds MSE-setting results with gains of 0.81–2.77 percentage points over corresponding MSE baselines. Table 7 adds direct-score results, such as 64.17±0.41 versus AdaConG's retained 66.53±0.55 for ResNet110/ResNet20. Matched pre-existing tables and empirical plots retain their results.

T1.justification: V4 removes the entire optimization derivation from v3 Appendix A.2, including weighted gradients, stationary-point conditions and the closed-form MSE solution in Equations 7–13. Although explicitly presented as illustrative rather than a formal performance proof, this is substantive mathematical reasoning. CP preliminaries and core objectives remain.

C1.justification: The principal adaptive-guidance contribution, evaluated application scope and over-sixfold navigation-reward claim remain. V4's Introduction additionally states that CP provides rigorous uncertainty estimates even when the underlying distribution changes, extending its explicit reliability claim.

C2.justification: V4 replaces v3 Appendix A.7's warning about exchangeability under strong shifts and its explicit soft-signal, rather than strict-coverage, interpretation. Exchangeability remains in the preliminaries, but the replacement Appendix A.5 instead discusses dependence on well-defined ground truth and possible ambiguous-label, credal-set and continual-learning extensions. This materially changes the qualification of the central uncertainty rationale.

D1.justification: V4 Section 3 and Appendix A.3 newly specify sliding-window RL calibration, N=1000, batches of m=128, imitation-policy initialization and EMA quantile updates; v3 only stated that the RL quantile updates online. V4 also removes Algorithm 1's pseudocode. Other documented preprocessing, training and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: V4 adds adaptive-CP references supporting its RL calibration discussion, references on ambiguous ground truth and imprecise probabilities, and additional robotics citations. It replaces the cited entropy reference. The main related-work narrative and first-framework positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 shortens the title, revises applicability terminology, replaces numbered main-text subsections with paragraph headings, and rewrites the RL calibration and final discussion passages. Appendix sections are reorganized, but most retained introductory, related-work and experimental prose closely matches v3.

P2.justification: Document-wide reformatting changes headers, title/author presentation, typography and figure/table placement. V3 Figure 1 is removed, while Figure 2 is redrawn and moved into the Introduction as v4 Figure 1. V4 adds Tables 3 and 7 and removes the algorithm display; existing empirical plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The new ablations strengthen empirical support, and the fuller RL calibration description improves reproducibility. However, v4 removes the optimization derivation and explicit qualifications about interpreting CP under strong shifts while strengthening its distribution-change statement. These substantive gains and losses leave the net direction of overall quality unclear.
